reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The new unit test checks only the internal JDBC type, leaving the reported updateRow() failure and persisted plaintext unverified for encrypted CHAR and VARCHAR with sendStringParametersAsUnicode=false.
1 open issue - [Add updateRow() regression coverage for encrypted CHAR and VARCHAR](https://github.com/microsoft/mssql-jdbc/pull/3096#discussion_r4522463301) · New
What changed in this PR Fixes #2303 by using the underlying encrypted column type to decide whether textual updates require hex decoding in the SQL Server JDBC driver. **Changes:** - Prevents encrypted CHAR/VARCHAR updates from being treated as binary values. - Preserves hex conversion for ordinary and encrypted binary columns. - Adds database-free unit tests for JDBC type selection. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | src/​test/​java/​com/​microsoft/​sqlserver/​jdbc/​ColumnAlwaysEncryptedUpdateTest.java | Adds mocked regression tests for encrypted text and binary updates. | | src/​main/​java/​com/​microsoft/​sqlserver/​jdbc/​Column.java | Uses encryption metadata’s base type for the hex-conversion decision. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: The new unit test checks only the internal JDBC type, leaving the reported `updateRow()` failure and persisted value untested. Add a regression in the existing Always Encrypted integration suite for CHAR and VARCHAR with `sendStringParametersAsUnicode=false`: update with non-hex text, call `updateRow()`, then re-query and assert the plaintext, accounting for CHAR padding. Keep the database-free unit test as well.
